4640 namespace Lean
4641 
4642 open BEq (beq)
4643 open HAdd (hAdd)
4644 
4645 /--
4646 Hierarchical names consist of a sequence of components, each of
4647 which is either a string or numeric, that are written separated by dots (`.`).
4648 
4649 Hierarchical names are used to name declarations and for creating
4650 unique identifiers for free variables and metavariables.
4651 
4652 You can create hierarchical names using a backtick:
4653 ```
4654 `Lean.Meta.whnf
4655 ```
4656 It is short for `.str (.str (.str .anonymous "Lean") "Meta") "whnf"`.
4657 
4658 You can use double backticks to request Lean to statically check whether the name
4659 corresponds to a Lean declaration in scope.
4660 ```
4661 ``Lean.Meta.whnf
4662 ```
4663 If the name is not in scope, Lean will report an error.
4664 
4665 There are two ways to convert a `String` to a `Name`:
4666 
4667  1. `Name.mkSimple` creates a name with a single string component.
4668 
4669  2. `String.toName` first splits the string into its dot-separated
4670     components, and then creates a hierarchical name.
4671 -/
4672 inductive Name where
4673   /-- The "anonymous" name. -/
4674   | anonymous : Name
4675   /--
4676   A string name. The name `Lean.Meta.run` is represented at
4677   ```lean
4678   .str (.str (.str .anonymous "Lean") "Meta") "run"
4679   ```
4680   -/
4681   | str (pre : Name) (str : String)
4682   /--
4683   A numerical name. This kind of name is used, for example, to create hierarchical names for
4684   free variables and metavariables. The identifier `_uniq.231` is represented as
4685   ```lean
4686   .num (.str .anonymous "_uniq") 231
4687   ```
4688   -/
4689   | num (pre : Name) (i : Nat)
4690 with
4691   /-- A hash function for names, which is stored inside the name itself as a
4692   computed field. -/
4693   @[computed_field, inline] hash : Name → UInt64
4694     | .anonymous => .ofNatLT 1723 (of_decide_eq_true rfl)
4695     | .str p s => mixHash p.hash s.hash
4696     | .num p v => mixHash p.hash (dite (LT.lt v UInt64.size) (fun h => UInt64.ofNatLT v h) (fun _ => UInt64.ofNatLT 17 (of_decide_eq_true rfl)))
4697 
4698 instance : Inhabited Name where
4699   default := Name.anonymous
4700 
4701 instance : Hashable Name where
4702   hash := Name.hash
4703 
4704 namespace Name
4705 
4706 /--
4707 `.str p s` is now the preferred form.
4708 -/
4709 @[export lean_name_mk_string]
4710 abbrev mkStr (p : Name) (s : String) : Name :=
4711   Name.str p s
4712 
4713 /--
4714 `.num p v` is now the preferred form.
4715 -/
4716 @[export lean_name_mk_numeral]
4717 abbrev mkNum (p : Name) (v : Nat) : Name :=
4718   Name.num p v
4719 
4720 /--
4721 Converts a `String` to a `Name` without performing any parsing. `mkSimple s` is short for `.str .anonymous s`.
4722 
4723 This means that `mkSimple "a.b"` is the name `«a.b»`, not `a.b`.
4724 -/
4725 abbrev mkSimple (s : String) : Name :=
4726   .str .anonymous s
4727 
4728 /-- Make name `s₁` -/
4729 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr1 (s₁ : String) : Name :=
4730   .str .anonymous s₁
4731 
4732 /-- Make name `s₁.s₂` -/
4733 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr2 (s₁ s₂ : String) : Name :=
4734   .str (.str .anonymous s₁) s₂
4735 
4736 /-- Make name `s₁.s₂.s₃` -/
4737 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr3 (s₁ s₂ s₃ : String) : Name :=
4738   .str (.str (.str .anonymous s₁) s₂) s₃
4739 
4740 /-- Make name `s₁.s₂.s₃.s₄` -/
4741 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr4 (s₁ s₂ s₃ s₄ : String) : Name :=
4742   .str (.str (.str (.str .anonymous s₁) s₂) s₃) s₄
4743 
4744 /-- Make name `s₁.s₂.s₃.s₄.s₅` -/
4745 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr5 (s₁ s₂ s₃ s₄ s₅ : String) : Name :=
4746   .str (.str (.str (.str (.str .anonymous s₁) s₂) s₃) s₄) s₅
4747 
4748 /-- Make name `s₁.s₂.s₃.s₄.s₅.s₆` -/
4749 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr6 (s₁ s₂ s₃ s₄ s₅ s₆ : String) : Name :=
4750   .str (.str (.str (.str (.str (.str .anonymous s₁) s₂) s₃) s₄) s₅) s₆
4751 
4752 /-- Make name `s₁.s₂.s₃.s₄.s₅.s₆.s₇` -/
4753 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr7 (s₁ s₂ s₃ s₄ s₅ s₆ s₇ : String) : Name :=
4754   .str (.str (.str (.str (.str (.str (.str .anonymous s₁) s₂) s₃) s₄) s₅) s₆) s₇
4755 
4756 /-- Make name `s₁.s₂.s₃.s₄.s₅.s₆.s₇.s₈` -/
4757 @[expose, reducible] def mkStr8 (s₁ s₂ s₃ s₄ s₅ s₆ s₇ s₈ : String) : Name :=
4758   .str (.str (.str (.str (.str (.str (.str (.str .anonymous s₁) s₂) s₃) s₄) s₅) s₆) s₇) s₈
4759 
4760 /-- (Boolean) equality comparator for names. -/
4761 @[extern "lean_name_eq"]
4762 protected def beq : (@& Name) → (@& Name) → Bool
4763   | anonymous, anonymous => true
4764   | str p₁ s₁, str p₂ s₂ => and (BEq.beq s₁ s₂) (Name.beq p₁ p₂)
4765   | num p₁ n₁, num p₂ n₂ => and (BEq.beq n₁ n₂) (Name.beq p₁ p₂)
4766   | _,         _         => false
4767 
4768 instance : BEq Name where
4769   beq := Name.beq
4770 
4771 /--
4772 This function does not have special support for macro scopes.
4773 See `Name.append`.
4774 -/
4775 @[expose] def appendCore : Name → Name → Name
4776   | n, .anonymous => n
4777   | n, .str p s => .str (appendCore n p) s
4778   | n, .num p d => .num (appendCore n p) d
4779 
4780 end Name
4781 
4782 /-- The default maximum recursion depth. This is adjustable using the `maxRecDepth` option. -/
4783 def defaultMaxRecDepth := 512
4784 
4785 /-- The message to display on stack overflow. -/
4786 def maxRecDepthErrorMessage : String :=
4787   "maximum recursion depth has been reached\n\
4788    use `set_option maxRecDepth <num>` to increase limit\n\
4789    use `set_option diagnostics true` to get diagnostic information"
4790 
4791 /-! # Syntax -/
4792 
4793 /--
4794 Source information that relates syntax to the context that it came from.
4795 
4796 The primary purpose of `SourceInfo` is to relate the output of the parser and the macro expander to
4797 the original source file. When produced by the parser, `Syntax.node` does not carry source info; the
4798 parser associates it only with atoms and identifiers. If a `Syntax.node` is introduced by a
4799 quotation, then it has synthetic source info that both associates it with an original reference
4800 position and indicates that the original atoms in it may not originate from the Lean file under
4801 elaboration.
4802 
4803 Source info is also used to relate Lean's output to the internal data that it represents; this is
4804 the basis for many interactive features. When used this way, it can occur on `Syntax.node` as well.
4805 -/
4806 inductive SourceInfo where
4807   /--
4808   A token produced by the parser from original input that includes both leading and trailing
4809   whitespace as well as position information.
4810 
4811   The `leading` whitespace is inferred after parsing by `Syntax.updateLeading`. This is because the
4812   “preceding token” is not well-defined during parsing, especially in the presence of backtracking.
4813   -/
4814   | original (leading : Substring.Raw) (pos : String.Pos.Raw) (trailing : Substring.Raw) (endPos : String.Pos.Raw)
4815   /--
4816   Synthetic syntax is syntax that was produced by a metaprogram or by Lean itself (e.g. by a
4817   quotation). Synthetic syntax is annotated with a source span from the original syntax, which
4818   relates it to the source file.
4819 
4820   The delaborator uses this constructor to store an encoded indicator of which core language
4821   expression gave rise to the syntax.
4822 
4823   The `canonical` flag on synthetic syntax is enabled for syntax that is not literally part of the
4824   original input syntax but should be treated “as if” the user really wrote it for the purpose of
4825   hovers and error messages. This is usually used on identifiers in order to connect the binding
4826   site to the user's original syntax even if the name of the identifier changes during expansion, as
4827   well as on tokens that should receive targeted messages.
4828 
4829   Generally speaking, a macro expansion should only use a given piece of input syntax in a single
4830   canonical token. An exception to this rule is when the same identifier is used to declare two
4831   binders, as in the macro expansion for dependent if:
4832   ```
4833   `(if $h : $cond then $t else $e) ~>
4834   `(dite $cond (fun $h => $t) (fun $h => $t))
4835   ```
4836   In these cases, if the user hovers over `h` they will see information about both binding sites.
4837   -/
4838   | synthetic (pos : String.Pos.Raw) (endPos : String.Pos.Raw) (canonical := false)
4839   /-- A synthesized token without position information. -/
4840   | protected none
4841 
4842 instance : Inhabited SourceInfo := ⟨SourceInfo.none⟩
4843 
4844 namespace SourceInfo
4845 
4846 /--
4847 Gets the position information from a `SourceInfo`, if available.
4848 If `canonicalOnly` is true, then `.synthetic` syntax with `canonical := false`
4849 will also return `none`.
4850 -/
4851 def getPos? (info : SourceInfo) (canonicalOnly := false) : Option String.Pos.Raw :=
4852   match info, canonicalOnly with
4853   | original (pos := pos) ..,  _
4854   | synthetic (pos := pos) (canonical := true) .., _
4855   | synthetic (pos := pos) .., false => some pos
4856   | _,                         _     => none
4857 
4858 /--
4859 Gets the end position information from a `SourceInfo`, if available.
4860 If `canonicalOnly` is true, then `.synthetic` syntax with `canonical := false`
4861 will also return `none`.
4862 -/
4863 def getTailPos? (info : SourceInfo) (canonicalOnly := false) : Option String.Pos.Raw :=
4864   match info, canonicalOnly with
4865   | original (endPos := endPos) ..,  _
4866   | synthetic (endPos := endPos) (canonical := true) .., _
4867   | synthetic (endPos := endPos) .., false => some endPos
4868   | _,                               _     => none
4869 
4870 /--
4871 Gets the substring representing the trailing whitespace of a `SourceInfo`, if available.
4872 -/
4873 def getTrailing? (info : SourceInfo) : Option Substring.Raw :=
4874   match info with
4875   | original (trailing := trailing) .. => some trailing
4876   | _                                  => none
4877 
4878 /--
4879 Gets the end position information of the trailing whitespace of a `SourceInfo`, if available.
4880 If `canonicalOnly` is true, then `.synthetic` syntax with `canonical := false`
4881 will also return `none`.
4882 -/
4883 def getTrailingTailPos? (info : SourceInfo) (canonicalOnly := false) : Option String.Pos.Raw :=
4884   match info.getTrailing? with
4885   | some trailing => some trailing.stopPos
4886   | none          => info.getTailPos? canonicalOnly
4887 
4888 end SourceInfo
4889 
4890 /--
4891 Specifies the interpretation of a `Syntax.node` value. An abbreviation for `Name`.
4892 
4893 Node kinds may be any name, and do not need to refer to declarations in the environment.
4894 Conventionally, however, a node's kind corresponds to the `Parser` or `ParserDesc` declaration that
4895 produces it. There are also a number of built-in node kinds that are used by the parsing
4896 infrastructure, such as `nullKind` and `choiceKind`; these do not correspond to parser declarations.
4897 -/
4898 abbrev SyntaxNodeKind := Name
4899 
4900 /-! # Syntax AST -/
4901 
4902 /--
4903 A possible binding of an identifier in the context in which it was quoted.
4904 
4905 Identifiers in quotations may refer to either global declarations or to namespaces that are in scope
4906 at the site of the quotation. These are saved in the `Syntax.ident` constructor and are part of the
4907 implementation of hygienic macros.
4908 -/
4909 inductive Syntax.Preresolved where
4910   /-- A potential namespace reference -/
4911   | namespace (ns : Name)
4912   /-- A potential global constant or section variable reference, with additional field accesses -/
4913   | decl (n : Name) (fields : List String)
4914 
4915 /--
4916 Lean syntax trees.
4917 
4918 Syntax trees are used pervasively throughout Lean: they are produced by the parser, transformed by
4919 the macro expander, and elaborated. They are also produced by the delaborator and presented to
4920 users.
4921 -/
4922 inductive Syntax where
4923   /--
4924   A portion of the syntax tree that is missing because of a parse error.
4925 
4926   The indexing operator on `Syntax` also returns `Syntax.missing` when the index is out of bounds.
4927   -/
4928   | missing : Syntax
4929   /--
4930   A node in the syntax tree that may have further syntax as child nodes. The node's `kind`
4931   determines its interpretation.
4932 
4933   For nodes produced by the parser, the `info` field is typically `Lean.SourceInfo.none`, and source
4934   information is stored in the corresponding fields of identifiers and atoms. This field is used in
4935   two ways:
4936    1. The delaborator uses it to associate nodes with metadata that are used to implement
4937       interactive features.
4938    2. Nodes created by quotations use the field to mark the syntax as synthetic (storing the result
4939       of `Lean.SourceInfo.fromRef`) even when its leading or trailing tokens are not.
4940   -/
4941   -- Remark: the `node` constructor did not have an `info` field in previous versions. This caused a
4942   -- bug in the interactive widgets, where the popup for `a + b` was the same as for `a`. The
4943   -- delaborator used to associate subexpressions with pretty-printed syntax by setting the (string)
4944   -- position of the first atom/identifier to the (expression) position of the subexpression. For
4945   -- example, both `a` and `a + b` have the same first identifier, and so their infos got mixed up.
4946   | node   (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (args : Array Syntax) : Syntax
4947   /--
4948   A non-identifier atomic component of syntax.
4949 
4950   All of the following are atoms:
4951    * keywords, such as `def`, `fun`, and `inductive`
4952    * literals, such as numeric or string literals
4953    * punctuation and delimiters, such as `(`, `)`, and `=>`.
4954 
4955   Identifiers are represented by the `Lean.Syntax.ident` constructor. Atoms also correspond to
4956   quoted strings inside `syntax` declarations.
4957   -/
4958   | atom   (info : SourceInfo) (val : String) : Syntax
4959   /--
4960   An identifier.
4961 
4962   In addition to source information, identifiers have the following fields:
4963   * `rawVal` is the literal substring from the input file
4964   * `val` is the parsed Lean name, potentially including macro scopes.
4965   * `preresolved` is the list of possible declarations this could refer to, populated by
4966     [quotations](lean-manual://section/quasiquotation).
4967   -/
4968   | ident  (info : SourceInfo) (rawVal : Substring.Raw) (val : Name) (preresolved : List Syntax.Preresolved) : Syntax
4969 
4970 /-- Create syntax node with 1 child -/
4971 def Syntax.node1 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
4972   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray1 a₁)
4973 
4974 /-- Create syntax node with 2 children -/
4975 def Syntax.node2 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ a₂ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
4976   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray2 a₁ a₂)
4977 
4978 /-- Create syntax node with 3 children -/
4979 def Syntax.node3 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ a₂ a₃ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
4980   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray3 a₁ a₂ a₃)
4981 
4982 /-- Create syntax node with 4 children -/
4983 def Syntax.node4 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
4984   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray4 a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄)
4985 
4986 /-- Create syntax node with 5 children -/
4987 def Syntax.node5 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
4988   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray5 a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅)
4989 
4990 /-- Create syntax node with 6 children -/
4991 def Syntax.node6 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅ a₆ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
4992   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray6 a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅ a₆)
4993 
4994 /-- Create syntax node with 7 children -/
4995 def Syntax.node7 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅ a₆ a₇ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
4996   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray7 a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅ a₆ a₇)
4997 
4998 /-- Create syntax node with 8 children -/
4999 def Syntax.node8 (info : SourceInfo) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅ a₆ a₇ a₈ : Syntax) : Syntax :=
5000   Syntax.node info kind (Array.mkArray8 a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₅ a₆ a₇ a₈)
5001 
5002 /--
5003 `SyntaxNodeKinds` is a set of `SyntaxNodeKind`, implemented as a list.
5004 
5005 Singleton `SyntaxNodeKinds` are extremely common. They are written as name literals, rather than as
5006 lists; list syntax is required only for empty or non-singleton sets of kinds.
5007 -/
5008 @[expose] def SyntaxNodeKinds := List SyntaxNodeKind
5009 
5010 /--
5011 Typed syntax, which tracks the potential kinds of the `Syntax` it contains.
5012 
5013 While syntax quotations produce or expect `TSyntax` values of the correct kinds, this is not
5014 otherwise enforced; it can easily be circumvented by direct use of the constructor.
5015 -/
5016 structure TSyntax (ks : SyntaxNodeKinds) where
5017   /-- The underlying `Syntax` value. -/
5018   raw : Syntax
5019 
5020 instance : Inhabited Syntax where
5021   default := Syntax.missing
5022 
5023 instance : Inhabited (TSyntax ks) where
5024   default := ⟨default⟩
5025 
5026 /-! # Builtin kinds -/
5027 
5028 /--
5029 The `` `choice `` kind is used to represent ambiguous parse results.
5030 
5031 The parser prioritizes longer matches over shorter ones, but there is not always a unique longest
5032 match. All the parse results are saved, and the determination of which to use is deferred
5033 until typing information is available.
5034 -/
5035 abbrev choiceKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `choice
5036 
5037 /--
5038 `` `null `` is the “fallback” kind, used when no other kind applies. Null nodes result from
5039 repetition operators, and empty null nodes represent the failure of an optional parse.
5040 
5041 The null kind is used for raw list parsers like `many`.
5042 -/
5043 abbrev nullKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `null
5044 
5045 /--
5046 The `` `group `` kind is used for nodes that result from `Lean.Parser.group`. This avoids confusion
5047 with the null kind when used inside `optional`.
5048 -/
5049 abbrev groupKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `group
5050 
5051 /--
5052 The pseudo-kind assigned to identifiers: `` `ident ``.
5053 
5054 The name `` `ident `` is not actually used as a kind for `Syntax.node` values. It is used by
5055 convention as the kind of `Syntax.ident` values.
5056 -/
5057 abbrev identKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `ident
5058 
5059 /-- `` `str `` is the node kind of string literals like `"foo"`. -/
5060 abbrev strLitKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `str
5061 
5062 /-- `` `char `` is the node kind of character literals like `'A'`. -/
5063 abbrev charLitKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `char
5064 
5065 /-- `` `num `` is the node kind of number literals like `42` and `0xa1` -/
5066 abbrev numLitKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `num
5067 
5068 /--
5069 `` `hexnum `` is the node kind of hexadecimal numbers like `ea10`
5070 without the `0x` prefix. Recall that `hexnum` is not a token and must be prefixed.
5071 For hexadecimal number literals, you should use `num` instead.
5072 Example: `syntax anchor := "#" noWs hexnum`.
5073  -/
5074 abbrev hexnumKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `hexnum
5075 
5076 /-- `` `scientific `` is the node kind of floating point literals like `1.23e-3`. -/
5077 abbrev scientificLitKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `scientific
5078 
5079 /-- `` `name `` is the node kind of name literals like `` `foo ``. -/
5080 abbrev nameLitKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `name
5081 
5082 /-- `` `fieldIdx `` is the node kind of projection indices like the `2` in `x.2`. -/
5083 abbrev fieldIdxKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `fieldIdx
5084 
5085 /--
5086 `` `hygieneInfo `` is the node kind of the `Lean.Parser.hygieneInfo` parser, which produces an
5087 “invisible token” that captures the hygiene information at the current point without parsing
5088 anything.
5089 
5090 They can be used to generate identifiers (with `Lean.HygieneInfo.mkIdent`) as if they were
5091 introduced in a macro's input, rather than by its implementation.
5092 -/
5093 abbrev hygieneInfoKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `hygieneInfo
5094 
5095 /--
5096 `` `interpolatedStrLitKind `` is the node kind of interpolated string literal
5097 fragments like `"value = {` and `}"` in `s!"value = {x}"`.
5098 -/
5099 abbrev interpolatedStrLitKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `interpolatedStrLitKind
5100 /--
5101 `` `interpolatedStrKind `` is the node kind of an interpolated string literal like `"value = {x}"`
5102 in `s!"value = {x}"`.
5103 -/
5104 abbrev interpolatedStrKind : SyntaxNodeKind := `interpolatedStrKind
5105 
5106 /-- Creates an info-less node of the given kind and children. -/
5107 @[inline, expose] def mkNode (k : SyntaxNodeKind) (args : Array Syntax) : TSyntax (.cons k .nil) :=
5108   ⟨Syntax.node SourceInfo.none k args⟩
5109 
5110 /-- Creates an info-less `nullKind` node with the given children, if any. -/
5111 -- NOTE: used by the quotation elaborator output
5112 @[inline, expose] def mkNullNode (args : Array Syntax := Array.empty) : Syntax :=
5113   mkNode nullKind args |>.raw
5114 
5115 namespace Syntax
5116 
5117 /--
5118 Gets the kind of a `Syntax.node` value, or the pseudo-kind of any other `Syntax` value.
5119 
5120 “Pseudo-kinds” are kinds that are assigned by convention to non-`Syntax.node` values:
5121 `identKind` for `Syntax.ident`, `` `missing `` for `Syntax.missing`, and the atom's string literal
5122 for atoms.
5123 -/
5124 def getKind (stx : Syntax) : SyntaxNodeKind :=
5125   match stx with
5126   | Syntax.node _ k _    => k
5127   -- We use these "pseudo kinds" for antiquotation kinds.
5128   -- For example, an antiquotation `$id:ident` (using Lean.Parser.Term.ident)
5129   -- is compiled to ``if stx.isOfKind `ident ...``
5130   | Syntax.missing     => `missing
5131   | Syntax.atom _ v    => Name.mkSimple v
5132   | Syntax.ident ..    => identKind
5133 
5134 /--
5135 Changes the kind at the root of a `Syntax.node` to `k`.
5136 
5137 Returns all other `Syntax` values unchanged.
5138 -/
5139 def setKind (stx : Syntax) (k : SyntaxNodeKind) : Syntax :=
5140   match stx with
5141   | Syntax.node info _ args => Syntax.node info k args
5142   | _                       => stx
5143 
5144 /--
5145 Checks whether syntax has the given kind or pseudo-kind.
5146 
5147 “Pseudo-kinds” are kinds that are assigned by convention to non-`Syntax.node` values:
5148 `identKind` for `Syntax.ident`, `` `missing `` for `Syntax.missing`, and the atom's string literal
5149 for atoms.
5150 -/
5151 def isOfKind (stx : Syntax) (k : SyntaxNodeKind) : Bool :=
5152   beq stx.getKind k
5153 
5154 /--
5155 Gets the `i`'th argument of the syntax node. This can also be written `stx[i]`.
5156 Returns `missing` if `i` is out of range.
5157 -/
5158 def getArg (stx : Syntax) (i : Nat) : Syntax :=
5159   match stx with
5160   | Syntax.node _ _ args => args.getD i Syntax.missing
5161   | _                    => Syntax.missing
5162 
5163 /-- Gets the list of arguments of the syntax node, or `#[]` if it's not a `node`. -/
5164 def getArgs (stx : Syntax) : Array Syntax :=
5165   match stx with
5166   | Syntax.node _ _ args => args
5167   | _                    => Array.empty
5168 
5169 /-- Gets the number of arguments of the syntax node, or `0` if it's not a `node`. -/
5170 def getNumArgs (stx : Syntax) : Nat :=
5171   match stx with
5172   | Syntax.node _ _ args => args.size
5173   | _                    => 0
5174 
5175 /--
5176 Assuming `stx` was parsed by `optional`, returns the enclosed syntax
5177 if it parsed something and `none` otherwise.
5178 -/
5179 def getOptional? (stx : Syntax) : Option Syntax :=
5180   match stx with
5181   | Syntax.node _ k args => match and (beq k nullKind) (beq args.size 1) with
5182     | true  => some (args.get!Internal 0)
5183     | false => none
5184   | _                    => none
5185 
5186 /-- Is this syntax `.missing`? -/
5187 def isMissing : Syntax → Bool
5188   | Syntax.missing => true
5189   | _ => false
5190 
5191 /-- Is this syntax a `node` with kind `k`? -/
5192 def isNodeOf (stx : Syntax) (k : SyntaxNodeKind) (n : Nat) : Bool :=
5193   and (stx.isOfKind k) (beq stx.getNumArgs n)
5194 
5195 /-- `stx.isIdent` is `true` iff `stx` is an identifier. -/
5196 def isIdent : Syntax → Bool
5197   | ident .. => true
5198   | _        => false
5199 
5200 /-- If this is an `ident`, return the parsed value, else `.anonymous`. -/
5201 def getId : Syntax → Name
5202   | ident _ _ val _ => val
5203   | _               => Name.anonymous
5204 
5205 /-- Retrieve the immediate info from the Syntax node. -/
5206 def getInfo? : Syntax → Option SourceInfo
5207   | atom info ..  => some info
5208   | ident info .. => some info
5209   | node info ..  => some info
5210   | missing       => none
5211 
5212 /-- Retrieve the left-most node or leaf's info in the Syntax tree. -/
5213 partial def getHeadInfo? : Syntax → Option SourceInfo
5214   | atom info _   => some info
5215   | ident info .. => some info
5216   | node SourceInfo.none _ args   =>
5217     let rec loop (i : Nat) : Option SourceInfo :=
5218       match decide (LT.lt i args.size) with
5219       | true => match getHeadInfo? (args.get!Internal i) with
5220          | some info => some info
5221          | none      => loop (hAdd i 1)
5222       | false => none
5223     loop 0
5224   | node info _ _ => some info
5225   | _             => none
5226 
5227 /-- Retrieve the left-most leaf's info in the Syntax tree, or `none` if there is no token. -/
5228 partial def getHeadInfo (stx : Syntax) : SourceInfo :=
5229   match stx.getHeadInfo? with
5230   | some info => info
5231   | none      => SourceInfo.none
5232 
5233 /--
5234 Get the starting position of the syntax, if possible.
5235 If `canonicalOnly` is true, non-canonical `synthetic` nodes are treated as not carrying
5236 position information.
5237 -/
5238 def getPos? (stx : Syntax) (canonicalOnly := false) : Option String.Pos.Raw :=
5239   stx.getHeadInfo.getPos? canonicalOnly
5240 
5241 /--
5242 Get the ending position of the syntax, if possible.
5243 If `canonicalOnly` is true, non-canonical `synthetic` nodes are treated as not carrying
5244 position information.
5245 -/
5246 partial def getTailPos? (stx : Syntax) (canonicalOnly := false) : Option String.Pos.Raw :=
5247   match stx, canonicalOnly with
5248   | atom (SourceInfo.original (endPos := pos) ..) .., _
5249   | atom (SourceInfo.synthetic (endPos := pos) (canonical := true) ..) _, _
5250   | atom (SourceInfo.synthetic (endPos := pos) ..) _,  false
5251   | ident (SourceInfo.original (endPos := pos) ..) .., _
5252   | ident (SourceInfo.synthetic (endPos := pos) (canonical := true) ..) .., _
5253   | ident (SourceInfo.synthetic (endPos := pos) ..) .., false
5254   | node (SourceInfo.original (endPos := pos) ..) .., _
5255   | node (SourceInfo.synthetic (endPos := pos) (canonical := true) ..) .., _
5256   | node (SourceInfo.synthetic (endPos := pos) ..) .., false => some pos
5257   | node _ _ args, _ =>
5258     let rec loop (i : Nat) : Option String.Pos.Raw :=
5259       match decide (LT.lt i args.size) with
5260       | true => match getTailPos? (args.get!Internal ((args.size.sub i).sub 1)) canonicalOnly with
5261          | some info => some info
5262          | none      => loop (hAdd i 1)
5263       | false => none
5264     loop 0
5265   | _, _ => none
5266 
5267 /--
5268 An array of syntax elements interspersed with the given separators.
5269 
5270 Separator arrays result from repetition operators such as `,*`.
5271 [Coercions](lean-manual://section/coercions) to and from `Array Syntax` insert or remove separators
5272 as required.
5273 
5274 The typed equivalent is `Lean.Syntax.TSepArray`.
5275 -/
5276 structure SepArray (sep : String) where
5277   /-- The array of elements and separators, ordered like
5278   `#[el1, sep1, el2, sep2, el3]`. -/
5279   elemsAndSeps : Array Syntax
5280 
5281 /--
5282 An array of syntax elements that alternate with the given separator. Each syntax element has a kind
5283 drawn from `ks`.
5284 
5285 Separator arrays result from repetition operators such as `,*`.
5286 [Coercions](lean-manual://section/coercions) to and from `Array (TSyntax ks)` insert or remove
5287 separators as required. The untyped equivalent is `Lean.Syntax.SepArray`.
5288 -/
5289 structure TSepArray (ks : SyntaxNodeKinds) (sep : String) where
5290   /-- The array of elements and separators, ordered like
5291   `#[el1, sep1, el2, sep2, el3]`. -/
5292   elemsAndSeps : Array Syntax
5293 
5294 end Syntax
5295 
5296 /--
5297 An array of syntaxes of kind `ks`.
5298 -/
5299 abbrev TSyntaxArray (ks : SyntaxNodeKinds) := Array (TSyntax ks)
5300 
5301 /-- Implementation of `TSyntaxArray.raw`. -/
5302 unsafe def TSyntaxArray.rawImpl : TSyntaxArray ks → Array Syntax := unsafeCast
5303 
5304 /-- Converts a `TSyntaxArray` to an `Array Syntax`, without reallocation. -/
5305 @[implemented_by TSyntaxArray.rawImpl]
5306 opaque TSyntaxArray.raw (as : TSyntaxArray ks) : Array Syntax := Array.empty
5307 
5308 /-- Implementation of `TSyntaxArray.mk`. -/
5309 unsafe def TSyntaxArray.mkImpl : Array Syntax → TSyntaxArray ks := unsafeCast
5310 
5311 /-- Converts an `Array Syntax` to a `TSyntaxArray`, without reallocation. -/
5312 @[implemented_by TSyntaxArray.mkImpl]
5313 opaque TSyntaxArray.mk (as : Array Syntax) : TSyntaxArray ks := Array.empty
5314 
5315 /-- Constructs a synthetic `SourceInfo` using a `ref : Syntax` for the span. -/
5316 def SourceInfo.fromRef (ref : Syntax) (canonical := false) : SourceInfo :=
5317   let noncanonical ref :=
5318     match ref.getPos?, ref.getTailPos? with
5319     | some pos, some tailPos => .synthetic pos tailPos
5320     | _,        _            => .none
5321   match canonical with
5322   | true =>
5323     match ref.getPos? true, ref.getTailPos? true with
5324     | some pos, some tailPos => .synthetic pos tailPos true
5325     | _,        _            => noncanonical ref
5326   | false => noncanonical ref
5327 
5328 /-- Constructs a synthetic `atom` with no source info. -/
5329 def mkAtom (val : String) : Syntax :=
5330   Syntax.atom SourceInfo.none val
5331 
5332 /-- Constructs a synthetic `atom` with source info coming from `src`. -/
5333 def mkAtomFrom (src : Syntax) (val : String) (canonical := false) : Syntax :=
5334   Syntax.atom (SourceInfo.fromRef src canonical) val
5335 
5336 /-! # Parser descriptions -/
5337 
5338 /--
5339 A `ParserDescr` is a grammar for parsers. This is used by the `syntax` command
5340 to produce parsers without having to `import Lean`.
5341 -/
5342 inductive ParserDescr where
5343   /-- A (named) nullary parser, like `ppSpace` -/
5344   | const  (name : Name)
5345   /-- A (named) unary parser, like `group(p)` -/
5346   | unary  (name : Name) (p : ParserDescr)
5347   /-- A (named) binary parser, like `orelse` or `andthen`
5348   (written as `p1 <|> p2` and `p1 p2` respectively in `syntax`) -/
5349   | binary (name : Name) (p₁ p₂ : ParserDescr)
5350   /-- Parses using `p`, then pops the stack to create a new node with kind `kind`.
5351   The precedence `prec` is used to determine whether the parser should apply given
5352   the current precedence level. -/
5353   | node (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (prec : Nat) (p : ParserDescr)
5354   /-- Like `node` but for trailing parsers (which start with a nonterminal).
5355   Assumes the lhs is already on the stack, and parses using `p`, then pops the
5356   stack including the lhs to create a new node with kind `kind`.
5357   The precedence `prec` and `lhsPrec` are used to determine whether the parser
5358   should apply. -/
5359   | trailingNode (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (prec lhsPrec : Nat) (p : ParserDescr)
5360   /--
5361   Parses the literal symbol.
5362 
5363   The symbol is automatically included in the set of reserved tokens ("keywords").
5364   Keywords cannot be used as identifiers, unless the identifier is otherwise escaped.
5365   For example, `"fun"` reserves `fun` as a keyword; to refer an identifier named `fun` one can write `«fun»`.
5366   Adding a `&` prefix prevents it from being reserved, for example `&"true"`.
5367 
5368   Whitespace before or after the atom is used as a pretty printing hint.
5369   For example, `" + "` parses `+` and pretty prints it with whitespace on both sides.
5370   The whitespace has no effect on parsing behavior.
5371   -/
5372   | symbol (val : String)
5373   /--
5374   Parses a literal symbol. The `&` prefix prevents it from being included in the set of reserved tokens ("keywords").
5375   This means that the symbol can still be recognized as an identifier by other parsers.
5376 
5377   Some syntax categories, such as `tactic`, automatically apply `&` to the first symbol.
5378 
5379   Whitespace before or after the atom is used as a pretty printing hint.
5380   For example, `" + "` parses `+` and pretty prints it with whitespace on both sides.
5381   The whitespace has no effect on parsing behavior.
5382 
5383   (Not exposed by parser description syntax:
5384   If the `includeIdent` argument is true, lets `ident` be reinterpreted as `atom` if it matches.)
5385   -/
5386   | nonReservedSymbol (val : String) (includeIdent : Bool)
5387   /-- Parses using the category parser `catName` with right binding power
5388   (i.e. precedence) `rbp`. -/
5389   | cat (catName : Name) (rbp : Nat)
5390   /-- Parses using another parser `declName`, which can be either
5391   a `Parser` or `ParserDescr`. -/
5392   | parser (declName : Name)
5393   /-- Like `node`, but also declares that the body can be matched using an antiquotation
5394   with name `name`. For example, `def $id:declId := 1` uses an antiquotation with
5395   name `declId` in the place where a `declId` is expected. -/
5396   | nodeWithAntiquot (name : String) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (p : ParserDescr)
5397   /-- A `sepBy(p, sep)` parses 0 or more occurrences of `p` separated by `sep`.
5398   `psep` is usually the same as `symbol sep`, but it can be overridden.
5399   `sep` is only used in the antiquot syntax: `$x;*` would match if `sep` is `";"`.
5400   `allowTrailingSep` is true if e.g. `a, b,` is also allowed to match. -/
5401   | sepBy  (p : ParserDescr) (sep : String) (psep : ParserDescr) (allowTrailingSep : Bool := false)
5402   /-- `sepBy1` is just like `sepBy`, except it takes 1 or more instead of
5403   0 or more occurrences of `p`. -/
5404   | sepBy1 (p : ParserDescr) (sep : String) (psep : ParserDescr) (allowTrailingSep : Bool := false)
5405   /--
5406   - `unicode("→", "->")` parses a symbol matching either `→` or `->`. Each symbol is reserved.
5407     The second symbol is an ASCII version of the first.
5408     The  `pp.unicode` option controls which is used when pretty printing.
5409   - `unicode("→", "->", preserveForPP)` is the same except for pretty printing behavior.
5410     When the `pp.unicode` option is enabled, then the pretty printer uses whichever symbol
5411     matches the underlying atom in the syntax.
5412     The intent is that `preserveForPP` means that the ASCII variant is preferred.
5413     For example, `fun` notation uses `preserveForPP` for its arrow; the delaborator chooses
5414     `↦` or `=>` depending on the value of `pp.unicode.fun`, letting users opt-in to formatting with `↦`.
5415     Note that `notation` creates a pretty printer preferring the ASCII version.
5416   -/
5417   | unicodeSymbol (val asciiVal : String) (preserveForPP : Bool)
5418 
5419 instance : Inhabited ParserDescr where
5420   default := ParserDescr.symbol ""
5421 
5422 /--
5423 Although `TrailingParserDescr` is an abbreviation for `ParserDescr`, Lean will
5424 look at the declared type in order to determine whether to add the parser to
5425 the leading or trailing parser table. The determination is done automatically
5426 by the `syntax` command.
5427 -/
5428 abbrev TrailingParserDescr := ParserDescr
5429 
5430 /-!
5431 Runtime support for making quotation terms auto-hygienic, by mangling identifiers
5432 introduced by them with a "macro scope" supplied by the context. Details to appear in a
5433 paper soon.
5434 -/
5435 
5436 /--
5437 A macro scope identifier is just a `Nat` that gets bumped every time we
5438 enter a new macro scope. Within a macro scope, all occurrences of identifier `x`
5439 parse to the same thing, but `x` parsed from different macro scopes will
5440 produce different identifiers.
5441 -/
5442 abbrev MacroScope := Nat
5443 /-- Macro scope used internally. It is not available for our frontend. -/
5444 def reservedMacroScope := 0
5445 /-- First macro scope available for our frontend -/
5446 def firstFrontendMacroScope := hAdd reservedMacroScope 1
5447 
5448 /--
5449 A `MonadRef` is a monad that has a `ref : Syntax` in the read-only state.
5450 This is used to keep track of the location where we are working; if an exception
5451 is thrown, the `ref` gives the location where the error will be reported,
5452 assuming no more specific location is provided.
5453 -/
5454 class MonadRef (m : Type → Type) where
5455   /-- Get the current value of the `ref` -/
5456   getRef      : m Syntax
5457   /-- Run `x : m α` with a modified value for the `ref` -/
5458   withRef {α} : Syntax → m α → m α
5459 
5460 export MonadRef (getRef)
5461 
5462 instance (m n : Type → Type) [MonadLift m n] [MonadFunctor m n] [MonadRef m] : MonadRef n where
5463   getRef        := liftM (getRef : m _)
5464   withRef ref x := monadMap (m := m) (MonadRef.withRef ref) x
5465 
5466 /--
5467 Replaces `oldRef` with `ref`, unless `ref` has no position info.
5468 This biases us to having a valid span to report an error on.
5469 -/
5470 def replaceRef (ref : Syntax) (oldRef : Syntax) : Syntax :=
5471   match ref.getPos? with
5472   | some _ => ref
5473   | _      => oldRef
5474 
5475 /--
5476 Run `x : m α` with a modified value for the `ref`. This is not exactly
5477 the same as `MonadRef.withRef`, because it uses `replaceRef` to avoid putting
5478 syntax with bad spans in the state.
5479 -/
5480 @[always_inline, inline]
5481 def withRef [Monad m] [MonadRef m] {α} (ref : Syntax) (x : m α) : m α :=
5482   bind getRef fun oldRef =>
5483   let ref := replaceRef ref oldRef
5484   MonadRef.withRef ref x
5485 
5486 /--
5487 If `ref? = some ref`, run `x : m α` with a modified value for the `ref` by calling `withRef`.
5488 Otherwise, run `x` directly.
5489 -/
5490 @[always_inline, inline]
5491 def withRef? [Monad m] [MonadRef m] {α} (ref? : Option Syntax) (x : m α) : m α :=
5492   match ref? with
5493   | some ref => withRef ref x
5494   | _        => x
5495 
5496 /-- A monad that supports syntax quotations. Syntax quotations (in term
5497     position) are monadic values that when executed retrieve the current "macro
5498     scope" from the monad and apply it to every identifier they introduce
5499     (independent of whether this identifier turns out to be a reference to an
5500     existing declaration, or an actually fresh binding during further
5501     elaboration). We also apply the position of the result of `getRef` to each
5502     introduced symbol, which results in better error positions than not applying
5503     any position. -/
5504 class MonadQuotation (m : Type → Type) extends MonadRef m where
5505   /-- Get the fresh scope of the current macro invocation -/
5506   getCurrMacroScope : m MacroScope
5507   /-- Get the context name used in Note `Macro Scope Representation`. -/
5508   getContext        : m Name
5509   /--
5510   Execute action in a new macro invocation context. This transformer should be
5511   used at all places that morally qualify as the beginning of a "macro call",
5512   e.g. `elabCommand` and `elabTerm` in the case of the elaborator. However, it
5513   can also be used internally inside a "macro" if identifiers introduced by
5514   e.g. different recursive calls should be independent and not collide. While
5515   returning an intermediate syntax tree that will recursively be expanded by
5516   the elaborator can be used for the same effect, doing direct recursion inside
5517   the macro guarded by this transformer is often easier because one is not
5518   restricted to passing a single syntax tree. Modelling this helper as a
5519   transformer and not just a monadic action ensures that the current macro
5520   scope before the recursive call is restored after it, as expected.
5521   -/
5522   withFreshMacroScope {α : Type} : m α → m α
5523 
5524 export MonadQuotation (getCurrMacroScope withFreshMacroScope)
5525 
5526 -- TODO: delete after rebootstrap
5527 @[inherit_doc MonadQuotation.getContext]
5528 abbrev MonadQuotation.getMainModule := @MonadQuotation.getContext
5529 
5530 /-- Construct a synthetic `SourceInfo` from the `ref` in the monad state. -/
5531 @[inline]
5532 def MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos [Monad m] [MonadRef m] : m SourceInfo :=
5533   return SourceInfo.fromRef (← getRef)
5534 
5535 instance [MonadFunctor m n] [MonadLift m n] [MonadQuotation m] : MonadQuotation n where
5536   getCurrMacroScope   := liftM (m := m) getCurrMacroScope
5537   getContext          := liftM (m := m) MonadQuotation.getContext
5538   withFreshMacroScope := monadMap (m := m) withFreshMacroScope
5539 
5540 /-!
5541 # Note [Macro Scope Representation]
5542 
5543 We represent a name with macro scopes as
5544 ```
5545 <actual name>._@.(<ctx>.<scopes>)*.<ctx>._hyg.<scopes>
5546 ```
5547 Example: suppose the context name is `Init.Data.List.Basic`, and name is `foo.bla`, and macroscopes [2, 5]
5548 ```
5549 foo.bla._@.Init.Data.List.Basic._hyg.2.5
5550 ```
5551 The delimiter `_hyg` is used just to improve the `hasMacroScopes` performance.
5552 
5553 The primary purpose of the context name is to differentiate macro scopes from different files as the
5554 numeric scopes are reset in each file. The current scope is always the right-most one. Scopes from
5555 multiple files may be collected when we execute a macro generated in an imported file in the current
5556 file.
5557 ```
5558 foo.bla._@.Init.Data.List.Basic.2.1.Init.Lean.Expr._hyg.4
5559 ```
5560 
5561 The delimiter `_hyg` is used just to improve the `hasMacroScopes` performance.
5562 In practice, we further specify the context name down to be unique per declaration so that the
5563 numeric scopes are not influenced by the elaboration of preceding declarations. This helps both with
5564 ensuring declaration names are more stable so that `prefer_native` can find the correct native
5565 symbol as well as making exported information in general more stable, avoiding rebuilds under the
5566 module system. Thus the actual encoding of the context name in the current implementation is
5567 ```
5568 <main module>.<uniq>._hygCtx
5569 ```
5570 where `<uniq>` is an identifier unique within the current module, set by
5571 `Command.withInitQuotContext`; see there for details. Thus we can assume the full context name to be
5572 unique throughout all modules and reset the numeric scopes whenever establishing a fresh context
5573 name.
5574 -/
5575 
5576 /-- Does this name have hygienic macro scopes? -/
5577 @[expose] def Name.hasMacroScopes : Name → Bool
5578   | str _ s => beq s "_hyg"
5579   | num p _ => hasMacroScopes p
5580   | _       => false
5581 
5582 private def eraseMacroScopesAux : Name → Name
5583   | .str p s   => match beq s "_@" with
5584     | true  => p
5585     | false => eraseMacroScopesAux p
5586   | .num p _   => eraseMacroScopesAux p
5587   | .anonymous => Name.anonymous
5588 
5589 /-- Remove the macro scopes from the name. -/
5590 @[export lean_erase_macro_scopes]
5591 def Name.eraseMacroScopes (n : Name) : Name :=
5592   match n.hasMacroScopes with
5593   | true  => eraseMacroScopesAux n
5594   | false => n
5595 
5596 private def simpMacroScopesAux : Name → Name
5597   | .num p i => Name.mkNum (simpMacroScopesAux p) i
5598   | n        => eraseMacroScopesAux n
5599 
5600 /-- Helper function we use to create binder names that do not need to be unique. -/
5601 @[export lean_simp_macro_scopes]
5602 def Name.simpMacroScopes (n : Name) : Name :=
5603   match n.hasMacroScopes with
5604   | true  => simpMacroScopesAux n
5605   | false => n
5606 
5607 /--
5608 A `MacroScopesView` represents a parsed hygienic name. `extractMacroScopes`
5609 will decode it from a `Name`, and `.review` will re-encode it. The grammar of a
5610 hygienic name is:
5611 ```
5612 <name>._@.(<module_name>.<scopes>)*.<mainModule>._hyg.<scopes>
5613 ```
5614 -/
5615 structure MacroScopesView where
5616   /-- The original (unhygienic) name. -/
5617   name       : Name
5618   /-- All the name components `(<module_name>.<scopes>)*` from the imports
5619   concatenated together. -/
5620   imported   : Name
5621   /-- The context name, a globally unique prefix. -/
5622   ctx        : Name
5623   /-- The list of macro scopes. -/
5624   scopes     : List MacroScope
5625 
5626 instance : Inhabited MacroScopesView where
5627   default := ⟨default, default, default, default⟩
5628 
5629 /-- Encode a hygienic name from the parsed pieces. -/
5630 def MacroScopesView.review (view : MacroScopesView) : Name :=
5631   match view.scopes with
5632   | List.nil      => view.name
5633   | List.cons _ _ =>
5634     let base := (Name.mkStr (Name.appendCore (Name.appendCore (Name.mkStr view.name "_@") view.imported) view.ctx) "_hyg")
5635     view.scopes.foldl Name.mkNum base
5636 
5637 private def assembleParts : List Name → Name → Name
5638   | .nil,                acc => acc
5639   | .cons (.str _ s) ps, acc => assembleParts ps (Name.mkStr acc s)
5640   | .cons (.num _ n) ps, acc => assembleParts ps (Name.mkNum acc n)
5641   | _,                   _   => panic "Error: unreachable @ assembleParts"
5642 
5643 private def extractImported (scps : List MacroScope) (mainModule : Name) : Name → List Name → MacroScopesView
5644   | n@(Name.str p str), parts =>
5645     match beq str "_@" with
5646     | true  => { name := p, ctx := mainModule, imported := assembleParts parts Name.anonymous, scopes := scps }
5647     | false => extractImported scps mainModule p (List.cons n parts)
5648   | n@(Name.num p _), parts => extractImported scps mainModule p (List.cons n parts)
5649   | _,                    _     => panic "Error: unreachable @ extractImported"
5650 
5651 private def extractMainModule (scps : List MacroScope) : Name → List Name → MacroScopesView
5652   | n@(Name.str p str), parts =>
5653     match beq str "_@" with
5654     | true  => { name := p, ctx := assembleParts parts Name.anonymous, imported := Name.anonymous, scopes := scps }
5655     | false => extractMainModule scps p (List.cons n parts)
5656   | n@(Name.num _ _), acc => extractImported scps (assembleParts acc Name.anonymous) n List.nil
5657   | _,                    _   => panic "Error: unreachable @ extractMainModule"
5658 
5659 private def extractMacroScopesAux : Name → List MacroScope → MacroScopesView
5660   | Name.num p scp, acc => extractMacroScopesAux p (List.cons scp acc)
5661   | Name.str p _  , acc => extractMainModule acc p List.nil -- str must be "_hyg"
5662   | _,                _   => panic "Error: unreachable @ extractMacroScopesAux"
5663 
5664 /--
5665   Revert all `addMacroScope` calls. `v = extractMacroScopes n → n = v.review`.
5666   This operation is useful for analyzing/transforming the original identifiers, then adding back
5667   the scopes (via `MacroScopesView.review`). -/
5668 def extractMacroScopes (n : Name) : MacroScopesView :=
5669   match n.hasMacroScopes with
5670   | true  => extractMacroScopesAux n List.nil
5671   | false => { name := n, scopes := List.nil, imported := Name.anonymous, ctx := Name.anonymous }
5672 
5673 /-- Add a new macro scope onto the name `n`, in the given `ctx`. -/
5674 def addMacroScope (ctx : Name) (n : Name) (scp : MacroScope) : Name :=
5675   match n.hasMacroScopes with
5676   | true =>
5677     let view := extractMacroScopes n
5678     match beq view.ctx ctx with
5679     | true  => Name.mkNum n scp
5680     | false =>
5681       { view with
5682         imported   := view.scopes.foldl Name.mkNum (Name.appendCore view.imported view.ctx)
5683         ctx := ctx
5684         scopes     := List.cons scp List.nil
5685       }.review
5686   | false =>
5687     Name.mkNum (Name.mkStr (Name.appendCore (Name.mkStr n "_@") ctx) "_hyg") scp
5688 
5689 /--
5690 Appends two names `a` and `b`, propagating macro scopes from `a` or `b`, if any, to the result.
5691 Panics if both `a` and `b` have macro scopes.
5692 
5693 This function is used for the `Append Name` instance.
5694 
5695 See also `Lean.Name.appendCore`, which appends names without any consideration for macro scopes.
5696 Also consider `Lean.Name.eraseMacroScopes` to erase macro scopes before appending, if appropriate.
5697 -/
5698 @[expose] def Name.append (a b : Name) : Name :=
5699   match a.hasMacroScopes, b.hasMacroScopes with
5700   | true, true  =>
5701     panic "Error: invalid `Name.append`, both arguments have macro scopes, consider using `eraseMacroScopes`"
5702   | true, false =>
5703     let view := extractMacroScopes a
5704     { view with name := appendCore view.name b }.review
5705   | false, true =>
5706     let view := extractMacroScopes b
5707     { view with name := appendCore a view.name }.review
5708   | false, false => appendCore a b
5709 
5710 instance : Append Name where
5711   append := Name.append
5712 
5713 /--
5714 Add a new macro scope onto the name `n`, using the monad state to supply the
5715 main module and current macro scope.
5716 -/
5717 @[inline] def MonadQuotation.addMacroScope {m : Type → Type} [MonadQuotation m] [Monad m] (n : Name) : m Name :=
5718   bind MonadQuotation.getContext fun ctx =>
5719   bind getCurrMacroScope fun scp =>
5720   pure (Lean.addMacroScope ctx n scp)
5721 
5722 namespace Syntax
5723 
5724 /-- Is this syntax a null `node`? -/
5725 def matchesNull (stx : Syntax) (n : Nat) : Bool :=
5726   stx.isNodeOf nullKind n
5727 
5728 /--
5729   Function used for determining whether a syntax pattern `` `(id) `` is matched.
5730   There are various conceivable notions of when two syntactic identifiers should be regarded as identical,
5731   but semantic definitions like whether they refer to the same global name cannot be implemented without
5732   context information (i.e. `MonadResolveName`). Thus in patterns we default to the structural solution
5733   of comparing the identifiers' `Name` values, though we at least do so modulo macro scopes so that
5734   identifiers that "look" the same match. This is particularly useful when dealing with identifiers that
5735   do not actually refer to Lean bindings, e.g. in the `stx` pattern `` `(many($p)) ``. -/
5736 def matchesIdent (stx : Syntax) (id : Name) : Bool :=
5737   and stx.isIdent (beq stx.getId.eraseMacroScopes id.eraseMacroScopes)
5738 
5739 /-- Is this syntax a node kind `k` wrapping an `atom _ val`? -/
5740 def matchesLit (stx : Syntax) (k : SyntaxNodeKind) (val : String) : Bool :=
5741   match stx with
5742   | Syntax.node _ k' args => and (beq k k') (match args.getD 0 Syntax.missing with
5743     | Syntax.atom _ val' => beq val val'
5744     | _                  => false)
5745   | _                     => false
5746 
5747 end Syntax
5748 
5749 namespace Macro
5750 
5751 /-- References -/
5752 -- TODO: make private again and make Nonempty instance no_expose instead after bootstrapping
5753 opaque MethodsRefPointed : NonemptyType.{0}
5754 
5755 set_option linter.missingDocs false in
5756 @[expose] def MethodsRef : Type := MethodsRefPointed.type
5757 
5758 instance : Nonempty MethodsRef := MethodsRefPointed.property
5759 
5760 /-- The read-only context for the `MacroM` monad. -/
5761 structure Context where
5762   /-- An opaque reference to the `Methods` object. This is done to break a
5763   dependency cycle: the `Methods` involve `MacroM` which has not been defined yet. -/
5764   methods        : MethodsRef
5765   /-- The quotation context name for `MonadQuotation.getContext`. -/
5766   quotContext    : Name
5767   /-- The current macro scope. -/
5768   currMacroScope : MacroScope
5769   /-- The current recursion depth. -/
5770   currRecDepth   : Nat := 0
5771   /-- The maximum recursion depth. -/
5772   maxRecDepth    : Nat := defaultMaxRecDepth
5773   /-- The syntax which supplies the position of error messages. -/
5774   ref            : Syntax
5775 
5776 /-- An exception in the `MacroM` monad. -/
5777 inductive Exception where
5778   /-- A general error, given a message and a span (expressed as a `Syntax`). -/
5779   | error             : Syntax → String → Exception
5780   /-- An unsupported syntax exception. We keep this separate because it is
5781   used for control flow: if one macro does not support a syntax then we try
5782   the next one. -/
5783   | unsupportedSyntax : Exception
5784 
5785 /-- The mutable state for the `MacroM` monad. -/
5786 structure State where
5787   /-- The global macro scope counter, used for producing fresh scope names. -/
5788   macroScope : MacroScope
5789   /-- The list of trace messages that have been produced, each with a trace
5790   class and a message. -/
5791   traceMsgs  : List (Prod Name String) := List.nil
5792   /-- Declaration names of expanded macros, for use with `shake`. -/
5793   private expandedMacroDecls : List Name := List.nil
5794   deriving Inhabited
5795 
5796 end Macro
5797 
5798 /--
5799 The `MacroM` monad is the main monad for macro expansion. It has the
5800 information needed to handle hygienic name generation, and is the monad that
5801 `macro` definitions live in.
5802 
5803 Notably, this is a (relatively) pure monad: there is no `IO` and no access to
5804 the `Environment`. That means that things like declaration lookup are
5805 impossible here, as well as `IO.Ref` or other side-effecting operations.
5806 For more capabilities, macros can instead be written as `elab` using `adaptExpander`.
5807 -/
5808 abbrev MacroM := ReaderT Macro.Context (EStateM Macro.Exception Macro.State)
5809 
5810 /--
5811 A `macro` has type `Macro`, which is a `Syntax → MacroM Syntax`: it
5812 receives an input syntax and is supposed to "expand" it into another piece of
5813 syntax.
5814 -/
5815 abbrev Macro := Syntax → MacroM Syntax
5816 
5817 namespace Macro
5818 
5819 instance : MonadRef MacroM where
5820   getRef     := bind read fun ctx => pure ctx.ref
5821   withRef    := fun ref x => withReader (fun ctx => { ctx with ref := ref }) x
5822 
5823 /-- Throw an `unsupportedSyntax` exception. -/
5824 def throwUnsupported {α} : MacroM α :=
5825   throw Exception.unsupportedSyntax
5826 
5827 /--
5828 Throw an error with the given message,
5829 using the `ref` for the location information.
5830 -/
5831 def throwError {α} (msg : String) : MacroM α :=
5832   bind getRef fun ref =>
5833   throw (Exception.error ref msg)
5834 
5835 /-- Throw an error with the given message and location information. -/
5836 def throwErrorAt {α} (ref : Syntax) (msg : String) : MacroM α :=
5837   withRef ref (throwError msg)
5838 
5839 /--
5840 Increments the macro scope counter so that inside the body of `x` the macro
5841 scope is fresh.
5842 -/
5843 @[inline] protected def withFreshMacroScope {α} (x : MacroM α) : MacroM α :=
5844   bind (modifyGet (fun s => (s.macroScope, { s with macroScope := hAdd s.macroScope 1 }))) fun fresh =>
5845   withReader (fun ctx => { ctx with currMacroScope := fresh }) x
5846 
5847 /-- Run `x` with an incremented recursion depth counter. -/
5848 @[inline] def withIncRecDepth {α} (ref : Syntax) (x : MacroM α) : MacroM α :=
5849   bind read fun ctx =>
5850   match beq ctx.currRecDepth ctx.maxRecDepth with
5851   | true  => throw (Exception.error ref maxRecDepthErrorMessage)
5852   | false => withReader (fun ctx => { ctx with currRecDepth := hAdd ctx.currRecDepth 1 }) x
5853 
5854 instance : MonadQuotation MacroM where
5855   getCurrMacroScope ctx := pure ctx.currMacroScope
5856   getContext        ctx := pure ctx.quotContext
5857   withFreshMacroScope   := Macro.withFreshMacroScope
5858 
5859 /-- Add a new macro scope to the name `n`. -/
5860 def addMacroScope (n : Name) : MacroM Name :=
5861   MonadQuotation.addMacroScope n
5862 
5863 /-- The opaque methods that are available to `MacroM`. -/
5864 structure Methods where
5865   /-- Expands macros in the given syntax. A return value of `none` means there
5866   was nothing to expand. -/
5867   expandMacro?      : Syntax → MacroM (Option Syntax)
5868   /-- Get the current namespace in the file. -/
5869   getCurrNamespace  : MacroM Name
5870   /-- Check if a given name refers to a declaration. -/
5871   hasDecl           : Name → MacroM Bool
5872   /-- Resolves the given name to an overload list of namespaces. -/
5873   resolveNamespace  : Name → MacroM (List Name)
5874   /-- Resolves the given name to an overload list of global definitions.
5875   The `List String` in each alternative is the deduced list of projections
5876   (which are ambiguous with name components). -/
5877   resolveGlobalName : Name → MacroM (List (Prod Name (List String)))
5878   deriving Inhabited
5879 
5880 /-- Implementation of `mkMethods`. -/
5881 unsafe def mkMethodsImp (methods : Methods) : MethodsRef :=
5882   unsafeCast methods
5883 
5884 /-- Make an opaque reference to a `Methods`. -/
5885 @[implemented_by mkMethodsImp]
5886 opaque mkMethods (methods : Methods) : MethodsRef
5887 
5888 instance : Inhabited MethodsRef where
5889   default := mkMethods default
5890 
5891 /-- Implementation of `getMethods`. -/
5892 unsafe def getMethodsImp : MacroM Methods :=
5893   bind read fun ctx => pure (unsafeCast (ctx.methods))
5894 
5895 /-- Extract the methods list from the `MacroM` state. -/
5896 @[implemented_by getMethodsImp] opaque getMethods : MacroM Methods
5897 
5898 /--
5899 `expandMacro? stx` returns `some stxNew` if `stx` is a macro,
5900 and `stxNew` is its expansion.
5901 -/
5902 def expandMacro? (stx : Syntax) : MacroM (Option Syntax) := do
5903   (← getMethods).expandMacro? stx
5904 
5905 /-- Returns `true` if the environment contains a declaration with name `declName` -/
5906 def hasDecl (declName : Name) : MacroM Bool := do
5907   (← getMethods).hasDecl declName
5908 
5909 /-- Gets the current namespace given the position in the file. -/
5910 def getCurrNamespace : MacroM Name := do
5911   (← getMethods).getCurrNamespace
5912 
5913   /-- Resolves the given name to an overload list of namespaces. -/
5914 def resolveNamespace (n : Name) : MacroM (List Name) := do
5915   (← getMethods).resolveNamespace n
5916 
5917 /--
5918 Resolves the given name to an overload list of global definitions.
5919 The `List String` in each alternative is the deduced list of projections
5920 (which are ambiguous with name components).
5921 
5922 Remark: it will not trigger actions associated with reserved names. Recall that Lean
5923 has reserved names. For example, a definition `foo` has a reserved name `foo.def` for theorem
5924 containing stating that `foo` is equal to its definition. The action associated with `foo.def`
5925 automatically proves the theorem. At the macro level, the name is resolved, but the action is not
5926 executed. The actions are executed by the elaborator when converting `Syntax` into `Expr`.
5927 -/
5928 def resolveGlobalName (n : Name) : MacroM (List (Prod Name (List String))) := do
5929   (← getMethods).resolveGlobalName n
5930 
5931 /-- Add a new trace message, with the given trace class and message. -/
5932 def trace (clsName : Name) (msg : String) : MacroM Unit := do
5933   modify fun s => { s with traceMsgs := List.cons (Prod.mk clsName msg) s.traceMsgs }
5934 
5935 end Macro
5936 
5937 export Macro (expandMacro?)
5938 
5939 namespace PrettyPrinter
5940 
5941 /--
5942 The unexpander monad, essentially `Syntax → Option α`. The `Syntax` is the `ref`,
5943 and it has the possibility of failure without an error message.
5944 -/
5945 abbrev UnexpandM := ReaderT Syntax (EStateM Unit Unit)
5946 
5947 /--
5948 Function that tries to reverse macro expansions as a post-processing step of delaboration.
5949 While less general than an arbitrary delaborator, it can be declared without importing `Lean`.
5950 Used by the `[app_unexpander]` attribute.
5951 -/
5952 -- a `kindUnexpander` could reasonably be added later
5953 abbrev Unexpander := Syntax → UnexpandM Syntax
5954 
5955 instance : MonadQuotation UnexpandM where
5956   getRef              := read
5957   withRef ref x       := withReader (fun _ => ref) x
5958   -- unexpanders should not need to introduce new names
5959   getCurrMacroScope   := pure 0
5960   getContext          := pure `_fakeMod
5961   withFreshMacroScope := id
5962 
5963 end PrettyPrinter
5964 
5965 end Lean
